mainTopic: When a נזיר may drink wine: one action or all of them, and whether the תנופה is required
overview: The amud opens with the end of the משנה, where רבי שמעון rules that once the blood of just one of the נזיר's קרבנות is sprinkled, he may drink wine and become טמא to the dead. The גמרא then brings a ברייתא. רבי אליעזר says the נזיר may drink wine only after all the actions are done, and the חכמים say one action is enough. The חכמים learn this from a גזירה שוה on the word 'אחר' ('after'). When the גמרא suggests he might need both actions, it answers that the גזירה שוה would then serve no purpose. Next, רב rules that the תנופה (waving) of the נזיר's offering is מעכב. The גמרא shows this cannot follow the רבנן, since for them even shaving is not required. So רב follows רבי אליעזר. His ruling is still needed: for כפרה, waving is only שירי מצוה, so we might have thought it is not required for the נזיר either.

steps.title: רבי שמעון: one sprinkling of blood is enough
steps.stepSummary: The משנה closes with רבי שמעון's view: once the blood of any one of the נזיר's קרבנות is sprinkled, he may drink wine and become טמא to the dead.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: once the blood of one of the offerings has been sprinkled for the נזיר, he is allowed to drink wine and to become impure from the dead.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the last line of the משנה. רבי שמעון says the נזיר's restrictions end as soon as the blood of just one of his קרבנות is sprinkled.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A נזיר finishing his term brings three קרבנות and shaves his hair. רבי שמעון holds that he does not need to wait for all of this. One sprinkling of blood already lifts the ban on wine and on טומאת מת.

keyTerms.meaning: was sprinkled (thrown onto the מזבח)
the bloods, meaning the blood of the קרבנות
became permitted
to become ritually impure from a dead body

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says:

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיוָן שֶׁנִּזְרַק עָלָיו אֶחָד מִן הַדָּמִים —
phrases.english: Once the blood of one of the offerings has been sprinkled on his behalf,
the nazir is permitted to drink wine
and to become impure from the dead.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי שמעון, the sprinkling of one קרבן's blood permits the נזיר to drink wine and to become טמא to the dead.

steps.title: A ברייתא: all the actions or just one
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens with a ברייתא. רבי אליעזר says the נזיר drinks wine only after all the actions, and the חכמים say after a single action.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: The רבנן taught: 'And afterward the נזיר may drink wine' means after all the actions. These are the words of רבי אליעזר. And the חכמים say: after a single action.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא about the פסוק 'and afterward the נזיר may drink wine.' רבי אליעזר and the חכמים disagree about what 'afterward' means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר reads 'afterward' as after everything: all the קרבנות and the shaving. The חכמים read it as after just one action. This means shaving is not required before he may drink wine.

keyTerms.meaning: the Talmud's discussion of the משנה
all the actions
a single action

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two sides. רבי אליעזר is the strict one, requiring ALL the actions. The חכמים are the lenient ones, requiring only ONE.

phrases.english: GEMARA: The Sages taught:
"And afterward the nazir may drink wine"
means after all the actions,
these are the words of Rabbi Eliezer.
And the Sages say: after a single action.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא with a מחלוקת about when the נזיר may drink wine, related to the משנה's ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי אליעזר, the נזיר drinks wine only after all the actions. According to the חכמים, one action is enough.

steps.title: What is the source for the חכמים?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what reason the חכמים have for saying one action is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of the רבנן?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of the חכמים' view. This sets up the next step, which gives the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plain words 'afterward the נזיר may drink wine' could easily mean after everything. So the חכמים need a source showing that one action is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: what is their reason?

phrases.english: What is the reason of the Rabbis?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the חכמים' view from Step 2.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source showing that 'afterward' means after a single action.

steps.title: A גזירה שוה on the word 'after'
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים learn from a גזירה שוה. Just as 'after he has shaven' refers to one action, 'afterward he may drink wine' also refers to one action.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is written here, 'And afterward the נזיר may drink wine,' and it is written there, 'after he has shaven his נזירות.' Just as there 'after' means after a single action, so too here 'after' means after a single action.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a גזירה שוה. The word 'after' appears in two nearby פסוקים, so it means the same thing in both.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the earlier פסוק, 'after he has shaven' clearly refers to one action, the shaving. Because the same word appears, 'afterward the נזיר may drink wine' also refers to one action. So the נזיר does not need to finish everything before drinking.

keyTerms.meaning: it is written here
and it is written there
his shaving, after he has shaven
a comparison between two פסוקים that share the same word

steps.whatToRemember: The חכמים learn from a גזירה שוה on 'אחר' that the נזיר may drink wine after one action, not only after all of them.

phrases.english: It is written here: "And afterward the nazir may drink wine,"
and it is written there: "after he has shaven his naziriteship."
Just as there "after" means after a single action,
phrases.notes: There, the single action is the shaving.

phrases.english: so too here, "after" means after a single action.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גזירה שוה from 'after he has shaven' (one action) to 'afterward the נזיר may drink wine' (one action).

steps.title: Maybe he needs both actions
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the reading: perhaps the נזיר may not drink until both actions are done.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say that he may not drink until there are both actions!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the חכמים. Maybe the פסוקים mean he must do both the קרבן and the shaving before drinking.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read simply, the two פסוקים together seem to point to two actions: the shaving and the קרבן. If so, the נזיר would need both, which comes close to רבי אליעזר's view. The challenge questions whether the גזירה שוה really proves that one is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: say (that perhaps), used to suggest another reading
until there is
both of them

phrases.english: Say that he may not drink until there are both!
phrases.notes: Both means the shaving and the offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the conclusion drawn in Step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that one action is enough for the נזיר to drink wine.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוקים might mean both actions are needed, not just one.

steps.title: Otherwise the גזירה שוה would be pointless
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers: if both actions were needed, there would be no reason for the גזירה שוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why do I need the גזירה שוה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the חכמים. If both actions were required, the גזירה שוה would add nothing, so it must be teaching that one action is enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plain reading already suggests needing everything. A גזירה שוה would only be needed to teach something new. The new point is that a single action is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: if so
why do I need it?

steps.whatToRemember: A גזירה שוה must teach something. Here it teaches that one action alone permits the נזיר to drink wine, as the חכמים say.

phrases.aramaic: אִי הָכִי, גְּזֵירָה שָׁוָה לְמָה לִי?
phrases.english: If so, why do I need the verbal analogy?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, גְּזֵירָה שָׁוָה לְמָה לִי
steps.terutzResolutionType: The challenge would leave the source with no purpose.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Perhaps both the shaving and the קרבן are needed before drinking wine.
steps.terutzMaskana: Since the גזירה שוה must teach something new, it teaches that a single action is enough.

steps.title: רב: waving holds back the נזיר
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that the תנופה of the נזיר's offering is מעכב. Without it, the נזיר is not yet released from his נזירות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: The waving of a נזיר's offering holds back his release.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new statement from רב. He says the waving done with the נזיר's offering must happen before the נזיר may drink wine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This moves from the dispute about how many actions are needed to one specific action, the תנופה. רב says this action is required for the release, so skipping it keeps the נזיר forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Waving: the כהן waves parts of the offering
Holds back; it is required, and without it the result does not happen
A person who took a vow to avoid wine, haircuts, and טומאת מת

phrases.english: Rav said:
Waving in the case of a nazirite holds back [his release].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic with a ruling by רב about one specific action, the תנופה. The next step asks how this ruling fits the dispute in the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The תנופה of the נזיר's offering is required before his prohibitions are lifted.

steps.title: Whose opinion does רב follow?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which side of the dispute between רבי אליעזר and the רבנן רב is following.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to whom did רב say this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which opinion רב's ruling fits. This question sets up the next two steps, which test each side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two opinions on the table. רבי אליעזר requires all the actions, and the רבנן require only one. The גמרא wants to know where רב's ruling fits.

keyTerms.meaning: According to whom? Which opinion does this follow?

phrases.english: According to whom?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks which opinion רב's statement follows.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רב follows רבי אליעזר or the רבנן.

steps.title: It cannot follow the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: If רב followed the רבנן, his statement would make no sense. They say even shaving does not hold the נזיר back, so waving surely would not.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say he follows the רבנן: the רבנן say even shaving does not hold him back. Is it even a question that waving does not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the first option, that רב follows the רבנן, and shows it does not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן say one action is enough, so even the תגלחת, the shaving, is not required. If shaving does not hold him back, the waving surely does not. So רב's ruling cannot fit the רבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (offers one possibility in order to test it)
The נזיר's shaving at the end of his נזירות
The Sages (here, the חכמים of the ברייתא)
Is it even a question? (it should obviously be the same)

phrases.english: If you say it follows the Rabbis,
the Rabbis say even shaving does not hold back;
is it even a question that waving [does not]?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the first possible answer to the question and rejects it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that רב follows the רבנן.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: קל וחומר logic: if shaving, which is more important, does not hold him back for the רבנן, waving surely does not. So רב cannot follow them.

steps.title: According to רבי אליעזר it seems obvious
steps.stepSummary: So רב must follow רבי אליעזר. But then his statement seems unnecessary, because רבי אליעזר already said all the actions are needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he follows רבי אליעזר. But that is obvious! רבי אליעזר said the נזיר drinks only after all the actions.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the second option, רבי אליעזר. It challenges this too: why would רב need to say something so obvious?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר requires every action, and waving is one of them. So רב's ruling looks like it adds nothing new. The problem is no longer a contradiction. It is that his statement seems unneeded.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (moves on to a different option)
It is obvious (why say it?)
But he already said!

phrases.english: Rather, it follows Rabbi Eliezer;
[but then] it is obvious, since Rabbi Eliezer said:
After all the actions!
phrases.notes: These are רבי אליעזר's words from the ברייתא in step 2.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Since the רבנן option failed, the גמרא tries רבי אליעזר and finds a new problem.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for רב's statement if it follows רבי אליעזר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי אליעזר already requires all the actions, waving included, so רב's ruling seems to teach nothing new.

steps.title: Why רב needed to say it
steps.stepSummary: Waving does not hold back כפרה for other offerings. So we might have thought it does not hold back the נזיר either. רב teaches that for the נזיר it does.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: since for כפרה the waving is only an extra part of the מצוה, here too it does not hold back. So רב teaches us that it does.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by showing that רב's statement is not obvious after all. It teaches something we could have gotten wrong.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For other offerings, waving is only שירי מצוה, an extra part of the מצוה. The כפרה still works without it. We might have applied that here and said waving does not count as one of 'all the actions' for the נזיר. רב teaches that according to רבי אליעזר, waving is required for the נזיר.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said (introduces a mistaken thought)
Atonement brought about by an offering
Leftover parts of a מצוה; extras that do not hold back the main result
He teaches us (the new point)

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי אליעזר, waving holds back the נזיר's release, even though it does not hold back כפרה for other offerings.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think waving is required for every offering. For כפרה it is only an extra part of the מצוה‎. רב's ruling is a special rule for the נזיר, according to רבי אליעזר.

phrases.english: You might have said:
since, with regard to atonement,
it is [only] a leftover part of the מצוה,
phrases.notes: He means the כפרה still works even if the waving was not done.

phrases.english: here too it should not hold back;
[so] he teaches us [that it does].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'it is obvious' challenge by showing what רב adds.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the statement is needed to block a reasonable but mistaken thought (מהו דתימא).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Because waving is only שירי מצוה for כפרה, it would not hold back the נזיר either.
steps.terutzMaskana: According to רבי אליעזר, waving is required for the נזיר's release.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב follows רבי אליעזר. He teaches that for the נזיר, waving is required, unlike its role in כפרה.
